facts.text: Bennington was named by Brigham Young after a Vermont town near his childhood home, and local LDS leader Evan M. later formalized the name.
Settled by Mormon pioneers in 1864, Bennington was officially organized as a church branch in 1866 and became the Bennington Ward in 1877.
Bennington sits at 6,008 feet above sea level in the Bear Lake Valley, about five miles north of Montpelier and 12 miles south of Georgetown.
The valley’s microclimate moderates weather but brings persistent fog and frost in winter and early spring, thanks to cold air drainage and lake influences.
Early settlers moved the townsite in 1873 to its current spot near Bennington Creek after harsh winters revealed the original location’s challenges.
Bennington’s fertile land, fed by the Bear River and Bear Lake, supports a short growing season that ends with early autumn chills.
